tasks.description: Compute heat index from temperature (C) and relative humidity using Rothfusz regression with C<->F conversion for each 5-minute sample.
Estimate Humidex (perceived temperature) by first computing dew point (Magnus formula) and then applying the Humidex equation.
Calculate dew point temperature from ambient temperature and relative humidity using the Magnus-Tetens approximation.
Compute absolute humidity (g/m3) from temperature and relative humidity to assess moisture load independent of air temperature.
Classify each reading into comfort categories (e.g., comfortable, warm, hot-humid) using configurable temperature and humidity thresholds.
Trigger alerts when temperature, humidity, or comfort index exceeds configured thresholds, with hysteresis to prevent alert chatter.
Detect temperature anomalies using a rolling mean and standard deviation (configurable window, e.g., 5 samples) and flag z-score outliers.
Detect humidity anomalies using a rolling mean and standard deviation (configurable window) and flag z-score outliers.
Apply CUSUM change-point detection on temperature to identify sudden shifts indicative of HVAC faults.
Flag sudden changes when 5-minute deltas in temperature or humidity exceed configurable thresholds.
Aggregate 5-minute readings into hourly mean, min, max, and standard deviation for compact storage and trend analysis.
Forecast next-hour temperature and humidity using simple exponential smoothing; output 12x5-minute ahead predictions and hourly average.
Detect sustained humidity rise (positive slope over N samples) without a corresponding temperature drop, indicating possible poor ventilation.
Monitor temperature slope (deg/hour) and flag risk when upward trend persists beyond threshold during monitored periods.
Compute consecutive duration that readings stay outside the comfort zone to quantify exposure time.
Validate timestamps are monotonic at ~5-minute intervals, enforce metadata value ranges, and flag implausible jumps relative to sensor accuracy.
